meta.title: Questions & Information Needed
meta.subtitle: The register of what must be settled before a decision can reasonably be made. Each question states what is already known (with an official source), what is not known, how to find out, and whether it blocks a decision.
meta.reading_guide: 'Blocking' means a decision that changes the architecture, the legal position or the risk profile cannot be made until the question is answered. 'Non-blocking' questions can be answered while work continues.
meta.source_policy: Only NFL and official club sources are cited. Where no official source exists, the cell is left blank and the item is carried on the Flagged for Review page.

questions.question: Is this platform for private analysis of games the owner bets on, or is it intended to publish lines that other people bet against (i.e. operate a book)?
questions.why_it_matters: The two answers produce completely different platforms. Publishing a line with a stake attached is a regulated activity in most jurisdictions; analysing one's own bets is not. Every downstream design decision - prize structure, 'rewards', public leaderboard - depends on this.
questions.decision_blocked: Reward design, whether the leaderboard is public or private, whether a wagering interface may ever be added, and the entire compliance workstream.

known.fact: The NFL publishes its official playing rules and rule changes through NFL Football Operations.
The NFL publishes official league statements, including policy positions, through NFL Communications.

unknown: Whether the platform will accept, hold or publish stakes.
Whether the leaderboard rewards real money, a points-based allowance, or recognition only.
Whether lines are made available to any third party.
how_to_obtain: Answer the question in one sentence to the platform owner.
If the answer is 'publish lines to others', commission a jurisdiction-specific gaming-licensing review before any line is published.
If the answer is 'private analysis', record that decision in this register so the leaderboard reward design can be settled.

questions.question: Which states or countries will any wagering activity be conducted from or into?
questions.why_it_matters: Sports-betting legality, licensing and tax treatment are jurisdiction-specific; a single global design can be illegal in a subset of target markets.
questions.decision_blocked: Whether any transactional feature may be built at all; the compliance gate in the release checklist.
unknown: Legal entity and location of the operator.
Target jurisdictions and whether they are permitted for the intended activity.
Whether geofencing, identity checks and responsible-gambling controls are required.
how_to_obtain: Obtain a written legal opinion or a licensed compliance review for each target jurisdiction.
Record the permitted activity type per jurisdiction in a compliance matrix before development continues.

questions.question: Do NFL rules or club policies restrict personnel with access to this platform from betting on games?
questions.why_it_matters: Personnel with access to non-public injury and line information can be subject to league restrictions that would materially change who may operate the system.
questions.decision_blocked: Who may be granted access to injury data and to unpublished lines.

known.fact: The NFL's official rulebook and rule-change summaries are published by NFL Football Operations.

unknown: The specific personnel policy section that applies to staff with access to the platform.
Whether the platform's operators are in scope.
how_to_obtain: Read the current rulebook section on gambling and personnel for the 2026 season.
Have counsel confirm applicability to the operating individuals and entities.

questions.question: What is the required history depth for back-testing (how many prior seasons of official data must be retained)?
questions.why_it_matters: Sample size drives every confidence interval on the site. Three seasons cannot distinguish skill from variance in NFL betting; one season cannot support a parlay strategy at all.
questions.decision_blocked: Validation gate G1 thresholds and the first leaderboard eligibility date.

known.fact: Official standings, schedules and player statistics are published by NFL.com for prior seasons, and the pipeline already ingests 2023-2026.

unknown: Minimum seasons required before a strategy may be scored as eligible.
Whether the owner will fund historical data that NFL.com does not publish at game level.
how_to_obtain: Decide the minimum sample size per strategy class and encode it as gate G1.
Extend the season list in scripts/lib/official.py if more history is needed - the fetcher already handles arbitrary seasons.

questions.question: Is per-game player-level data (box score / game book) required, and is it acceptable to source it only from NFL.com game pages?
questions.why_it_matters: Player-prop strategies and any player-prop combination cannot be evaluated at all without game-level player logs, and the correlation matrix for prop combos is computed from them.
questions.decision_blocked: Whether the player-prop and prop-combination strategy classes can ever pass validation.

known.fact: NFL.com publishes the official player-statistics tables by category and season.
NFL.com publishes the official weekly schedule and results, which is the game-level index used to build box-score URLs.

unknown: Whether official game books (PDF) are the preferred per-game source or the HTML box score.
Whether per-game data must be retained for every season back to the chosen start year.
Whether the owner's own game logs may supplement official data (they may not, under the no-inference rule).
how_to_obtain: Run the box-score fetcher over one completed season and measure coverage against the official schedule.
Confirm the per-game field set required for each prop market the owner wants to trade.

questions.question: How deep should official depth-chart ingestion go, and who is responsible for keeping it correct?
questions.why_it_matters: The requirement to know when a second, third or fourth string replaces a starter is only satisfiable if the depth ordering is sourced, not inferred. Club depth charts are maintained by each club and are frequently stale or formatted differently.
questions.decision_blocked: The precision of the deficiency signal and therefore the size of the injury-related edge.

known.fact: Official club websites publish their own depth charts; the pipeline probes all 32 official club domains and keeps only pages that resolve.
The official NFL injury report lists, per team, the players reported for each game and their practice and game status.

unknown: Which clubs publish a machine-readable depth chart and which do not.
Whether a human curator will correct the gaps, and at what cadence.
Whether the official game book 'substitutions' order should be used as the fallback depth signal.
how_to_obtain: Run the depth-chart coverage check across all 32 clubs and publish the coverage table.
Agree a fallback order: official club depth chart, then official game-book starters and substitutions, then blank-and-flag.
questions.owner: Data engineering (with owner approval of the fallback rule)

questions.question: What is the decision-time stamp for each piece of information, and how far back must snapshots be retained?
questions.why_it_matters: Back-testing that uses a Saturday injury report for a Thursday game is look-ahead bias and will manufacture edge that does not exist.
questions.decision_blocked: Every back-test and therefore every leaderboard row.

known.fact: The official NFL injury report is published per week and lists each reported player's practice participation and game status.

unknown: The exact release time used as the decision stamp (NFL injury reports are released in windows).
How many weeks of historical snapshots must be retained for a valid back-test.
how_to_obtain: Add a per-week snapshot archive keyed by the official report URL and the fetch timestamp.
Adopt the conservative rule: a snapshot may only inform a decision after its recorded fetch time.

questions.question: What is the minimum sample size and the maximum acceptable drawdown for each strategy class?
questions.why_it_matters: These are the numbers that decide who wins the competition. Without them, the leaderboard ranks luck.
questions.decision_blocked: Gate thresholds G1, G5 and the reward split.
unknown: Minimum bets for a single-bet strategy, for a parlay strategy and for a prop-combo strategy.
Maximum tolerable peak-to-trough drawdown in units or percent of bankroll.
Whether a minimum live (out-of-sample) period is required in addition to a back-test.
how_to_obtain: Start from the gate table published on the Strategies page and adjust the thresholds there.
Confirm the thresholds before the first reward cycle is funded.

questions.question: How is skill separated from luck, quantitatively, and what threshold must be cleared?
questions.why_it_matters: This is the core of the brief. A strategy that is lucky looks identical to a skilled strategy on a win/loss record; only variance decomposition and out-of-sample consistency separate them.
questions.decision_blocked: Eligibility for rewards; the ranking order of the leaderboard.
unknown: The agreed skill-share threshold and the bootstrap interval width that satisfies it.
Whether the skill metric is computed per strategy in isolation or against a portfolio of all deployed strategies.
how_to_obtain: Adopt the published skill-share definition (model-implied variance divided by total observed variance) and set the threshold.
Confirm with a stress test: re-run the harness with a synthetic pure-luck strategy and confirm it is rejected.

questions.question: May the evaluation reference an independent market consensus, or must every strategy be judged only against our own lines?
questions.why_it_matters: Judging a strategy against our own line is circular: our line is produced by the same family of models. Without an independent reference the leaderboard can only measure self-consistency, not skill.
questions.decision_blocked: The validity of the entire leaderboard.

known.fact: The platform's own lines are generated from official NFL data; no third-party line feed is ingested, which is the required 'originate our own lines' property.

unknown: Whether an independent closing-line reference may be consulted for evaluation only (not for line generation).
If not, what objective reference replaces it - for example a held-out model trained on a different feature set and period.
how_to_obtain: Option A: permit a market reference for evaluation only, with the line-generation path proven independent.
Option B: adopt a two-model design where a separately specified evaluator, trained on a disjoint period and feature set, produces the reference probability.
Option C: restrict rewards to strategies that beat a null model with a pre-registered significance threshold.

questions.question: What is the minimum acceptable correlation between a new strategy and the strategies already deployed?
questions.why_it_matters: A cluster of highly correlated strategies multiplies exposure and makes the leaderboard look diversified when it is not.
questions.decision_blocked: How many strategies may be rewarded at once, and the decorrelation rule for parlay legs.
unknown: The correlation threshold above which a new strategy is treated as a duplicate.
Whether the correlation is computed on returns, on signals, or on both.
how_to_obtain: Adopt the published correlation matrix method and set the threshold in the gate table.
Verify against the computed matrix published on the Strategies page.

questions.question: What is the intended bankroll and stake-sizing policy, including whether fractional Kelly is acceptable?
questions.why_it_matters: Stake sizing changes every performance metric in the leaderboard, and an unbounded policy can bankrupt a strategy that is genuinely skilled.
questions.decision_blocked: Reward sizing and the drawdown gate.
unknown: Bankroll per strategy and total.
Stake fraction per bet, and whether a hard per-bet cap applies.
Whether parlays are staked flat or scaled by leg count.
how_to_obtain: Publish a stake policy with the platform, then encode it in the back-test harness.
Confirm whether the published metrics are per-unit or bankroll-normalised.

questions.question: What is the reward pool, its funding source, and the payout cadence?
questions.why_it_matters: A leaderboard without rewards is a report, not a competition; the brief asks for a competition that rewards top performers.
questions.decision_blocked: The competition launch date and the eligibility rules.
unknown: Pool size and periodicity.
Whether rewards are money, an allocation of the platform's own bankroll, or recognition.
Tie-break rule when two strategies have identical composite scores.
how_to_obtain: Fund and publish the reward schedule, or change the competition framing to a non-monetary scoreboard.
Publish the tie-break rule in the leaderboard specification before the first cycle closes.

questions.question: Who is eligible to submit a strategy, and may the same person submit strategies in more than one class?
questions.why_it_matters: Determines whether the leaderboard is an open field or a single-operator research log, and how correlated submissions are handled.
questions.decision_blocked: Entrant rules and the correlation clustering policy.
unknown: Whether the competition is open to other people or is an internal research competition.
Whether one entrant may occupy multiple leaderboard positions.
how_to_obtain: Decide and publish the entrant rules on the Leaderboard page.
Confirm whether a single entrant may have more than one strategy eligible in the same cycle.

questions.question: Must every hypothesis ever tested be disclosed, including the failures?
questions.why_it_matters: Multiple-testing disclosure is the only defence against publishing a lucky strategy that was found by trying thousands of things.
questions.decision_blocked: Whether the leaderboard may be presented as a skill ranking at all.
unknown: Whether a rejected-hypothesis register will be maintained.
The maximum number of hypotheses permitted per cycle and the multiple-testing correction to be applied.
how_to_obtain: Adopt a hypothesis register in the repository, with every tested hypothesis recorded whether it passed or failed.
Apply a Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate control across the hypothesis register.

questions.question: Which decisions is this platform meant to support, and what is the explicit decision that each output feeds?
questions.why_it_matters: Without a named decision per output, the site becomes a data dump. Each page should end in an action.
questions.decision_blocked: The information architecture of the site and the required fields on every page.
unknown: The primary decision: which games to bet, what price to accept, which strategy to fund, or all three.
Whether the owner wants a single ranked recommendation per game or a raw feed to choose from.
how_to_obtain: Answer in one sentence per output family; the site is then reorganised around those decisions.
Validate the answer by naming the action that follows from a given page.

questions.question: How should suggestions be prioritised when they conflict, and who has the final say?
questions.why_it_matters: The brief asks for a suggestions section so a reviewer can choose the best path. A prioritisation rule is what makes that review fast.
questions.decision_blocked: The ranking order of the Suggestions page.
unknown: Whether impact, cost, risk or reversibility dominates the ordering.
Who approves a suggestion and whether approval is recorded on the site.
how_to_obtain: Adopt the published default ordering (impact, then reversibility, then cost) and change it if another rule is preferred.
Record each approval on the Suggestions page so the board of record is visible.

questions.question: What counts as an acceptable official source when the NFL does not publish a datum (for example roster status codes)?
questions.why_it_matters: The verification rule is 'official site only'. Where no official source exists the value must be blank, which means some useful fields will permanently be blank unless a rule is set.
questions.decision_blocked: Which fields appear on the depth page at all.

known.fact: The NFL publishes the official injury report, standings, schedules, statistics and team/player pages on nfl.com.

unknown: Whether an official club's own site counts as an official source for roster status (the pipeline treats it as official and labels it as a club source).
Whether the NFL Players Association or NFL Enterprises pages may be used for contract and roster context.
how_to_obtain: Confirm the source hierarchy to publish on the Sources page.
Any datum without a confirmed official source stays blank and appears on the Flagged for Review page.

questions.question: Should the platform ever ingest non-official data, and if so, how is it labelled so it can never be confused with verified data?
questions.why_it_matters: The verification rule is the integrity of the whole site. A strict official-only policy is simplest, but it may block prop markets that need finer granularity.
questions.decision_blocked: The data-tier design and the labelling rules on every table.
unknown: Whether a second, clearly separated tier (for example 'model estimate' or 'owner-supplied') is permitted.
If permitted, whether tier-two data may ever appear on a decision page.
how_to_obtain: Adopt the published two-tier rule: official-verified data is publishable; anything else is labelled and quarantined.
Decide whether the leaderboard may ever be computed from non-official inputs (recommended: no).

questions.question: How often should the site refresh, and what is the acceptable staleness for an injury-driven decision?
questions.why_it_matters: The official injury report changes several times a week. A stale injury table is worse than no injury table because it looks current.
questions.decision_blocked: The scheduled cadence and the staleness warning thresholds.

known.fact: The official NFL injury report is a weekly publication covering all games, with practice participation and game status per player.

unknown: The maximum acceptable age of the injury snapshot before the site refuses to show it as current.
Whether the owner wants intraday refreshes around NFL release windows.
how_to_obtain: Adopt the published freshness policy and its warning banner.
Adjust the cron schedule in .github/workflows/data-pipeline.yml if intraday refreshes are wanted.

questions.question: What is the expected weekly maintenance load for depth-chart and injury review, and who performs it?
questions.why_it_matters: Automation covers retrieval, not verification. If a human must review depth charts weekly, that is a real recurring cost and must be planned for.
questions.decision_blocked: Whether depth resolution is fully automated or human-in-the-loop.
unknown: Hours per week expected for manual verification.
Whether an exception queue (only flagged items need review) is acceptable.
how_to_obtain: Run the depth coverage report for one week and count the number of clubs that need manual resolution.
Proceed with an exception-only workflow if the count is manageable.

questions.question: What is the retention and archival policy for official snapshots and back-test artefacts?
questions.why_it_matters: Reproducing a past leaderboard result requires the exact snapshot and the exact code that consumed it.
questions.decision_blocked: Storage plan and the audit model for the leaderboard.
unknown: Retention period and storage location for raw official payloads.
Whether every leaderboard row is regenerated on demand or archived as a signed artefact.
how_to_obtain: Adopt the published retention rule and store the artefacts with the code version.
Confirm storage capacity with the repository owner.

questions.question: Which markets are in scope: spread, moneyline, total, and which player-prop types?
questions.why_it_matters: Each market needs different data granularity and has a different correlation structure. Defining scope prevents building a half-supported prop model.
questions.decision_blocked: The line model output, the strategy register and the required official data fields.
unknown: Whether props include passing yards, rushing yards, receptions, receiving yards, touchdowns, sacks, interceptions, fantasy points.
Whether first-half and player-vs-player prop markets are wanted.
Whether the platform prices only the pre-game market or also live in-game.
how_to_obtain: Name the markets in priority order.
For each market, confirm that the official per-game field needed to evaluate it exists (link to Q-005).

questions.question: How should games with limited history (a new coaching staff, a new quarterback) be handled?
questions.why_it_matters: Team-level season-to-date ratings are exactly wrong for rebuilt teams, and NFL rosters change between seasons more than any other major sport.
questions.decision_blocked: Shrinkage design in the line model and the treatment of these games in the back-test.

known.fact: Official league standings publish points for and points against for every team, which are the inputs to a season-to-date strength model.

unknown: The minimum games before a team's rating is trusted.
Whether prior-year ratings may be carried forward, and with what weight.
how_to_obtain: Adopt a published shrinkage rule and test it in the harness.
Report the shrinkage weight on the methodology page so the assumption is visible.

questions.question: What is the house margin the platform's own lines should carry, and is the platform price-only or price-and-stake?
questions.why_it_matters: A published line without a stated margin is not actionable, and the margin determines whether a strategy can exist at all.
questions.decision_blocked: The line model output format and the reward mechanics.
unknown: Target hold per line (for example 2% to 4%).
Whether the platform takes the other side of a bet it quotes, or only publishes a price.
Whether a stake is offered alongside the price.
how_to_obtain: Set the margin in the line model configuration and publish it.
Decide the quoting model before any external publication.

questions.question: Who signs off on a strategy moving from research to funded deployment?
questions.why_it_matters: A model registry with no approval step lets an overfitted strategy reach real stakes.
questions.decision_blocked: The approval workflow for the leaderboard.
unknown: Whether the owner approves alone or a second reviewer is required.
Whether approval is per strategy, per class, or per cycle.
how_to_obtain: Publish the approval rule on the Leaderboard page and record each approval.
Until this is answered, no strategy may be marked funded.

questions.question: What is the change-control process for the line model, the strategy set and the published thresholds?
questions.why_it_matters: A silent threshold change mid-cycle invalidates the leaderboard. The repository already treats shared outputs as integration-only; the same rule should apply to model parameters.
questions.decision_blocked: Whether a cycle may be re-scored after a model change.
unknown: Whether model changes mid-cycle force a re-score or start a new cycle.
Whether the published gates are versioned and linked from the leaderboard.
how_to_obtain: Adopt the published rule: any change to the line model or the gates starts a new cycle and does not re-score a closed one.
Version the gate table and link the version from each leaderboard row.

questions.question: How will the owner verify the published numbers independently, and against which comparison page?
questions.why_it_matters: The brief requires links for manual review. The comparison page must be named so that a discrepancy is detectable.
questions.decision_blocked: The Sources page layout and the row-level links.

known.fact: Every published dataset row carries the official URL it was read from, and the page states the fetch timestamp and the SHA-256 of the raw payload.

unknown: Which comparison page the owner will use to reconcile (for example the NFL.com injury report page for the current week).
Whether the owner wants an on-page reconciliation count (rows published versus rows on the official page).
how_to_obtain: Publish the reconciliation count on each data page.
Record the owner's chosen comparison page in the Sources page.
